Espionage is supposed to be a secretive business, and spies are supposed to be virtually invisible. That hasn’t been the case for Alice Huang, the mysterious Shanghai executive who formed a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang, the founder of Nvidia, one of America’s most powerful tech companies.Many questions have arisen since it emerged that US intelligence believes that Huang (no relation of Jensen’s) is an asset recruited by the Chinese intelligence services to spy on behalf of Beijing. This morning’s newsletter explains what we know about the story, and what it tells us about the effectiveness of Chinese espionage. unclustered.title: Linkpost: "Neural Networks Are Already Clean" Followup Technical Paper
unclustered.summary: Yesterday, Goodfire released the companion technical report to Nick Cammarata’s viral interpretability essay "Neural Networks Are Already Clean", but it seems to have gotten buried in all the recent crazy AI news.The technical report is titled: "Neurons as an Interpretable Basis". Goodfire's Twitter announcement for it can be found here.Like Nick Cammarata's essay, it's full of inventive, oft-interactive data displays. Don't just feed this to an AI agent and assume they can grok the post by pulling a PDF.Quoting from the Abstract: (emphasis mine)We study the neurons of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B using sparsification methods, attribution tools, and research agents, and find three properties that make neurons interpretable units of computation:First, they are already functionally sparse. Ablating the 92.2% weakest MoE neuron activations for each forward pass has only modest effects on model capabilities – a 2.9% increase in language model loss.Second, neurons have relatively few semantic groupings
unclustered.headline: Goodfire Releases Technical Report on Neural Network Interpretability

More than 5000 of the assets are made by us, and the rest is from different open source asset stores that we put in one place that is searchable through a CLI and MCP (free) so Codex can access everything in the toolbox easily. These assets, can be used for games or websites you make with codex and are cc0 license so you can grab them and use them commercially! We also open-sourced systems like procedural dungeons, physics engines, crowd navigation, car driving mechanics, procedural terrain generation, tree generators etc. so codex can start from bigger blocks instead of building everything from scratch. These blocks can then be edited in any way to look completely different than the system itself Link: https://patch.gg/create/toolbox/assets Note: Viewing the library requires no sign-in or download. unclustered.title: Chips for Humanity: Compute for AI safety research
unclustered.summary: TLDR: Compute will likely be a bottleneck in short-timelines, so I am helping launch Chips for Humanity. Please fill out our survey to inform us of your compute needs if you work in AI safety.Our Theory of ChangeIf timelines are short (I personally believe they are short...but I also know one should not make sweeping statements in a pseudo corporate type of post), a lot of the most important safety research will happen around "crunchtime" (no better way to define this than: when things start getting Serious), and a lot of it will be done by AI. That research runs on compute, compute may be scarce by then, and grant money moves slowly. So we will secure compute ahead of time and get it to third party safety researchers quickly.In More Detail:I believe third party AI safety research is where tokens and compute will be importation when things get serious and as we approach crunchtime. This research will need tokens from closed source models, for AI labor and experiments, and also compute
